usage: 종류 = type/category; the form always asks this
받다 is the natural verb, not 가지다
만료되다 = to expire; key word at immigration
D-2; just say the purpose + 비자 in daily speech
examples: 만료돼요 is the spoken form of 만료되다
What visa did you enter on?
officer's question; 들어오다 = enter the country
I have to go to immigration because of my visa.
nuance: 비자 is the everyday loanword; people rarely say the formal 사증 in conversation. In daily life you name the purpose and add 비자 (워홀 비자, 결혼 비자) rather than the official D/F codes. With officials, pair it with 만료되다 (expire) and 연장하다 (extend).
mistakes: Saying 비자를 가지다 to mean 'get a visa' — use 비자를 받다 or 비자를 신청하다
Confusing 비자 (visa) with 여권 (passport); they are different documents

usage: the official term for your visa category
asked on entry cards and forms
합법 = legal; opposite is 불법 체류
examples: polite formula 어떻게 되세요? for asking official info
I extended my period of stay by 6 months.
Be careful not to fall into illegal stay.
되지 않게 = so that it doesn't become
nuance: 체류 is bureaucratic and almost always appears in fixed compounds (체류 자격, 체류 기간, 체류 연장) rather than alone. You will see it constantly on HiKorea and at the immigration office. Knowing 체류 자격 (your visa status) is essential when an official asks 체류 자격이 어떻게 되세요?.
mistakes: Using 체류 for a short tourist 'stay at a hotel' — that is 숙박 or just 머무르다
Saying 체류증; the actual card is 외국인등록증, while 체류 자격 is the abstract status

usage: 신청 = application; the core admin pairing
the reason most foreigners use this word
examples: 비자 연장 신청은 만료 전에 해야 해요.
You must apply for a visa extension before it expires.
I want to extend the contract by one more year.
The extension application could be rejected.
nuance: 연장 covers extending almost any time-bound thing: visas, lease contracts (계약 연장), library books, deadlines. For immigration it is almost always 체류 연장 or 비자 연장. The verb 연장하다 is what you'll say at the counter or type on the booking site.
mistakes: Confusing 연장 (extension) with 갱신 (renewal) — 갱신 is reissuing a new card, 연장 is adding more time
Dropping 신청 and just saying 연장 주세요 at the counter; say 연장하고 싶어요 or 연장 신청하러 왔어요

usage: must be within 14 days of moving
to go file a move-in report
examples: When you move, you must file a move-in report within 14 days.
I'm on my way to the community center to file a move-in report.
전입신고를 해야 확정일자를 받을 수 있어요.
You can only get a fixed date stamp after filing a move-in report.
nuance: 전입신고 is a must-do for residents: report your new address at the local 주민센터 within 14 days of moving. For renters it is tied to 확정일자, which protects your deposit, so locals treat it as urgent. Foreigners usually do it in person at the 주민센터 or immigration, often alongside updating their 외국인등록증.
mistakes: Confusing 전입신고 (reporting where you moved IN) with 전출 (moving OUT) — you normally only file 전입신고
Thinking it's optional; missing the 14-day deadline can bring a fine

usage: the full name; 등본 is the short form
떼다 is THE verb for pulling official documents
examples: Please issue me just one copy of the extract.
한 통만 = just one copy; 떼다 used at the counter
My company says to submit the resident extract.
You can also get the extract from the self-service kiosk.
nuance: 등본 (short for 주민등록등본) lists everyone registered at your address and is requested constantly — for jobs, bank accounts, contracts. The idiomatic verb is 떼다 (to pull/issue), not 받다: 등본 떼러 가요. Foreigners get the equivalent 외국인등록사실증명, but everyone still says 등본 colloquially.
mistakes: Using 받다 instead of 떼다 for getting the document — natives say 등본을 떼다
Confusing 등본 (household list) with 초본 (your personal address history); offices ask for one specifically

usage: full name; people shorten to 출입국
the office where you handle visa matters
심사 = screening at the airport counter
examples: Foreigner registration is done at the immigration office.
Make your immigration appointment on HiKorea.
Get your passport ready in front of the immigration counter.
nuance: 출입국 literally means 'exit-entry' and is the everyday short name for the 출입국·외국인청/사무소, where you handle visas, registration, and extensions. You almost always need a reservation via HiKorea before going. At the airport, the same word appears in 출입국 심사 (passport control).
mistakes: Assuming you can walk in — most 출입국 tasks require a 하이코리아 reservation first
Confusing 출입국 (the office/process) with 출국 (departing) and 입국 (arriving), which are one-directional

usage: for bank cards, ID cards, transit cards
verb form; note the 받다 ending
examples: I lost my residence card, so I have to get it reissued.
How many days does debit card reissuance take?
며칠 걸려요? = how many days does it take
Please fill out the reissuance application form.
작성하다 = to fill out a form
nuance: 재발급 is what you ask for when something is lost, stolen, or damaged — bank cards, ID, residence card, transit card. Use the verb 재발급받다 (to have it reissued) for yourself, or 재발급해 주세요 to ask staff. Compare 갱신 (renewal when something simply expires), which is a different request.
mistakes: Using 재발급 when the document merely expired — that's 갱신 (renewal)
Saying 재발급하다 about yourself; the receiver says 재발급받다, the office 재발급해 주다

usage: to fill out an application form
작성하다 is the right verb, not 쓰다 here
내다 = to hand in (casual for 제출하다)
examples: Please fill out this application form first.
Don't forget to sign the application form.
Submit the completed form at that window over there.
nuance: 신청서 is any fill-in application form, from visa extensions to library cards. The collocation verb is 작성하다 (fill out), which sounds more correct than 쓰다 in offices. To hand it in, staff say 내세요 or 제출하세요. You'll hear 신청서 작성해 주세요 at virtually every Korean counter.
mistakes: Using 쓰다 instead of 작성하다 for completing a form in formal settings
Confusing 신청서 (the form you fill in) with 신청 (the act of applying)

usage: 하다-verb; what you do at the counter
처 = place; where you hand things in
the number you get after applying
examples: Until what time can I submit the documents?
We'll text you once the intake is complete.
Pull a number ticket at the reception desk over there.
번호표 뽑다 = take a queue ticket
nuance: 접수 is the bureaucratic word for an office accepting and logging your application or documents. At a hospital or office you 접수하다 first, then wait for your number. 접수가 됐어요 means your paperwork is officially in the system. It's slightly formal but used everywhere from clinics to government windows.
mistakes: Confusing 접수 (intake/submission) with 영수증 (a payment receipt) — different 'receipt'
Saying 접수받다 when you mean to submit; you 접수하다, the office 접수받다

usage: to be issued / to get issued
the charge for producing the document
examples: The residence card is issued a few days later.
I'd like to be issued one copy of the certificate.
증명서 = certificate; 한 통 = one copy
여기서 임시 카드를 즉시 발급해 드려요.
We issue a temporary card on the spot here.
임시 = temporary; 발급해 드리다 humble form
nuance: 발급 is the official act of producing/handing over a card or certificate. Say 발급받다 about getting one yourself, 발급해 주세요 when asking staff, and 발급돼요/발급됩니다 for the passive 'it gets issued'. It appears on every Korean kiosk and counter (즉시 발급, 무인 발급).
mistakes: Saying 발급하다 about yourself; the citizen 발급받다 while the office 발급하다/발급해 주다
Mixing up 발급 (issuing a new one) with 재발급 (reissuing a lost one) and 갱신 (renewing)

usage: for a fee to be incurred
the charge to produce a document
examples: How much is the reissuance fee?
A fee gets added when you transfer money.
There's no separate fee for this application.
따로 없다 = there isn't a separate one
nuance: 수수료 is the catch-all word for an administrative or service charge — bank transfers, card reissuance, document issuance, booking platforms. You 수수료를 내다 (pay it) and it 붙다/들다 (gets added/incurred). It's distinct from 요금 (usage charge like fares/bills) and 세금 (tax).
mistakes: Confusing 수수료 (service/processing fee) with 요금 (usage charge) or 세금 (tax)
Saying 수수료를 사다; you 수수료를 내다 (pay) or it 든다 (costs)

usage: what staff ask you to do
examples: Could you show me your ID, please?
For foreigners, the residence card is the ID.
신분증을 안 가져와서 접수를 못 했어요.
I couldn't submit it because I didn't bring my ID.
nuance: 신분증 is the umbrella term for any government photo ID — 주민등록증, 운전면허증, passport, or for residents the 외국인등록증. You'll be asked 신분증 있으세요? at banks, pharmacies, offices, and when buying alcohol/cigarettes. Always carry one; many counter tasks (접수, 발급) require ID verification first.
mistakes: Thinking 신분증 means only the Korean 주민등록증; your 외국인등록증 or passport counts
Confusing 신분증 (ID) with 신청서 (application form); they sound similar to beginners
